name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 158 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 22% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Tamil Nadu.
status.nb: 158 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 22 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Tamil Nadu.

summary.en: Security forces in Jammu and Kashmir are intensifying a hunt for 65 foreign terrorists while the Union Home Secretary and the IB Director are scheduled to visit for a high-level security review. In Manipur, security forces killed a suspected KCP cadre, apprehended eight others in an encounter, and separately arrested six militants while the Assam Rifles expanded community outreach. The state reported that deaths from spurious liquor have risen to 20, with nine arrested persons remanded to police custody. In Chhattisgarh’s Bastar region, caches containing arms, night-vision equipment, a drone and cash were seized, and three Maoist dumps were recovered in Bijapur. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Jammu og Kashmir intensiverer jakten på 65 utenlandske terrorister mens unionens hjemdepartementssekretær og IB-direktøren er planlagt å besøke for en høyt nivå sikkerhetsgjennomgang. I Manipur drepte sikkerhetsstyrker en mistenkt KCP-medlem, pågrepet åtte andre i en sammenstøt, og arresterte separat seks militante mens Assam Rifles utvidet samfunnskontakten. Staten rapporterte at dødsfall fra falsk alkohol har steget til 20, med ni arresterte personer som er satt i politiets varetekt. I Chhattisgarh sin Bastar-region ble lager med våpen, nattkikkere, en drone og kontanter beslaglagt, og tre maoist-lagre ble funnet i Bijapur. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
